transcript:
This is NPR News Now, the latest headlines every hour.
Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Cora Coleman.
President Trump campaigned last night in Iowa's conservative 4th Congressional District.
Iowa Public Radio's Sheila Brummer reports from Sioux City the focus was on Iowa's Senate race.
Supporters of President Trump filled an aircraft hangar and spilled outside to watch him speak Thursday evening.
They responded enthusiastically to his call for a Republican victory in Iowa.
If you get out and vote like you did in 2024, we win in the landslide, you know. We win in the landslide.
Two years ago, Trump carried this date by more than 13 points.
But this year's election comes as some farmers in Iowa struggle with high fuel and fertilizer costs.
Trump says a Democratic pickup here could make it harder for him to advance his agenda during his final two years.
We'll show the race is a tight one.
For NPR News, I'm Sheila Brummer in Sioux City, Iowa.
A federal judge has ordered that President Trump must answer questions under oath by December 11th.
This is part of a lawsuit that Trump himself filed against British broadcaster the BBC.
Trump is demanding $10 billion for the BBC's alleged defamation.
The BBC has apologized for a documentary that spliced two separate parts of a Trump speech together from January 6th, 2021 and gave an impression he'd made a direct call for violence, which he rejects.
Trump was supposed to answer questions last Friday in the case, but pulled out.
NPR's David Folkenflick says Trump's lawyers cited matters of national importance.
Trump's private attorney invoked the idea yesterday that president does a lot of more things than you could possibly know.
The BBC's lead attorney said, hey, that's fake news.
He noted that last Friday Trump campaigned with a Republican Senate candidate in Dalton, Georgia, then went to Mar-a-Lago for an event with the Republican National Committee.
The Madrid judge said, nope, let's do this. You're going to have to do this by December 11th.
Discovery is supposed to wrap up by a week later.
NPR's David Folkenflick reporting.
The Justice Department has indicted a prominent Virginia Democrat on charges, including racketeering, money laundering and conspiracy to distribute marijuana.
From VPM News, Jad Khalil has more.
It made the FBI rated a cannabis dispensary connected to the senior Democrat in the Virginia Senate, Eloise Lucas.
The indictment alleges she and others used their businesses to sell illegal marijuana.
It also alleges she used her position to enrich herself by working to legalize marijuana.
The 82-year-old Lucas, who is black and a frequent critic of Republicans, said in a statement she grew up under Jim Crow and has, quote, "seen what happens when people in power try to silence those who stand up to them."
Attorney General Todd Blanche rejected allegations that politics influenced the investigation, saying the probe into Lucas began before the Trump administration took office.
For NPR News, I'm Jad Khalil in Richmond, Virginia.
You're listening to NPR News.
Drugmaker Merck has released early some much-awaited clinical data.
These look at the effectiveness of mRNA vaccines and the serious skin cancer melanoma.
The data show the vaccine treatment can't substantially slow down both the recurrence of the cancer and death from it.
NPR's Yuki Noguchi reports Merck and its partner Moderna will use this data to apply for regulatory approval.
The medical community has been awaiting release of this data, which is the largest study to date gauging the effectiveness of mRNA vaccine technology against cancer.
In this case, vaccines are designed and personalized based on each person's melanoma tumor sample.
Over the two-year study period, those drugs reduced the risk of occurrence or death among patients by 42 percent compared to the standard immunotherapy treatment alone. Moreover, the study found that adding the vaccine did not increase significant side effects.
Yuki Noguchi, NPR News.
Minnesota officials claim the Justice Department has stopped sharing information into the investigation of the shooting deaths of two Americans earlier this year.
The activists, Renee Goode and Alex Priddy, died after being shot by federal agents.
ICE agents had been deployed to Minnesota to arrest suspected migrants.
Minnesota officials say they need the information to build a case.
Justice Department officials say that decision to share is up to them.
A slow-moving storm in the Southwest has triggered flood watches and warnings in Utah, Colorado and New Mexico this morning.
This is NPR.

Federal judge orders Trump to answer questions under oath by December 11 in BBC lawsuit
Justice Department indicts Virginia Democratic senator Eloise Lucas on racketeering and marijuana charges
Merck releases early data showing mRNA melanoma vaccine does not substantially slow cancer recurrence
Minnesota officials say Justice Department stopped sharing information on fatal federal agent shootings
Slow-moving Southwest storm triggers flood watches and warnings in Utah, Colorado, New Mexico
